preview: Sayali Panch shares her FTE interview experience for Graduate Analyst at Deutsche Bank, detailing the online coding test, two technical rounds, a professional fitment interview, and an HR round.
content: Deutsche Bank FTE interview experience 2024 Sayali Panch B.Tech in Information Technology Details ● CTC: 19.63 LPA ● Role: Graduate Analyst ● Eligibility: CGPA above 7; No Backlogs; CS, IT & EXTC branch Hiring Pattern ● Online Coding Test ● Technical Interview - 1 ● Technical Interview - 2 ● Professional Fitment interview ● HR interview Online Coding Round : ● Platform: Proctored on HackerEarth ● Date: 4th August 2023 ● Questions: 3 with partial test case marks ● Duration: 1.5 hours 1 1. Power Limit - 20 marks [Solved by brute force] Given two resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have to select one resource out of the two to run the software. The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second, the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of the unselected resource gets increased by 1. The software stops when at least one resource has a power of 0. You are given integers A and B. Print the maximum number of seconds your software can run if you select the resources optimally as output. Sample input: 3 5 Sample output: 6 Passed all test cases. 2. Auto Suggest - 50 marks [Solved by DP] Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word S. All the words and the query word S consist of lowercase alphabets only. You need to auto suggest the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S. Two words are first compared by their Levenshtein distance to the word S. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given priority. Levenshtein Distance is defined as the minimum number of edits required to convert one string to another. Operations allowed to edit are insert, delete or replace a character. Input: N words S 2 Output: suggested word Passed all test cases. 3. Backlink Sorting - 50 marks [created 2 dictionaries sorted one and used it] You are given N webpage titles and corresponding arrays that constrain the number of backlinks for each webpage. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order based on the number of backlinks they have. If two or more pages have the same number of links then maintain their ordering. Sample Input: 4 pg1 pg2 pg3 pg4 20 80 40 10 Sample Output: pg2 pg3 pg1 pg4 Passed all test cases. 40 students shortlisted for interviews held on 9th August 2023 in offline mode in TPO Technical Interview - 1 : ● Tell me about yourself ● He told me he was from the OS domain and asked if I was comfortable with that subject, I said yes. 3 ● Asked me to draw the architecture between end user and os (the kernel diagram one) and explain it. ● Difference between Linux and Ubuntu, then compare it with windows. ● List all the linux commands you know (asked the implementation of some) ● Told me to list all the memory units I knew in ascending order. ● Asked me which memory can be accessed fastest by CPU and then gave me various options and asked to order them ( RAM, CD, Hard disk, cache something like that) ● Asked me how a small RAM can run a large program, I answered using virtual memory, then he asked to explain what virtual memory is. ● Asked me about paging and segmentation and to state different types of page replacement algorithms. Gave a numerical for optimal page replacement. ● Asked me to write any code in any language just it should have a practical application and gave example of olx (I didn’t understand what he wanted but I wrote a python code for student and course management) ● List all the git commands you know, then he asked some follow up questions like can you create branch of branch etc. ● Asked me if I had any questions. Lasted for about 45 min to 1 hr. 33 shortlisted for round 2. Technical Interview - 2 : ● Again introduce. Then asked which language I prefer. ● Write a code to reverse a string ● Asked about stacks and told to code it. ● Code to find prime no. in a given range ● What is a binary tree? 4 State all the tree traversal methods you know, then show inorder traversal. Asked which traversal has the best complexity and what it is. ● Write sql query to create a table of given specifications (with distinct, primary key and all), insert data in it. Then gave some conditions to fetch particular data. ● What is OOPS, state pillars. Told to show each pillar implementation for Library management System and explain. ● What is an abstract class? difference between abstract class and interface ● Asked me about my projects in depth and the technologies used ● What are sockets and some other basic CN questions. ● Asked me a puzzle similar to this: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/missionaries-and-cannibals/ Lasted 1 hr Professional Fitness Interview : ● Introduce but include something not on resume ● Tell about internship experience and the project done there (explained the entire project in depth). Asked me why I was not taking SAP Labs PPO ● Then asked about all the committees I was part of like Coc and my role there. ● What is normalization, its different forms and conditions. ● Then gave me some scenarios and asked what would I do ● Asked if I could handle a leadership role ● Asked what my father does and about family background ● Asked if I wanted to pursue higher education and if yes what. (I answered that I was not sure but after gaining some experience maybe I could do MBA finance as this role would give me finance domain knowledge) 5 Lasted 45 min. 26 shortlisted for HR HR Interview : ● Introduce yourself. ● Internship discussion, how was Bangalore, team, what did you learn, highlight on some learning you gained excluding technical and overall experience. ● Why DB, if you get PPO from SAP Labs would you accept (I said no), why not? ● Where do you see yourself in 5 years? ● Are you comfortable with relocation Lasted 25 - 30 min All 26 candidates were selected. Tips: ● For DSA practice leetcode questions and follow any code sheet. I also referred to Geeks for Geeks. ● Practice all the core CS subjects from most asked interview questions. (like from interviewbit) ● If there is any ambiguity in understanding question, ask them and clarify, ● Know all your projects mentioned in the resume and their tech stack thoroughly. Do not lie on your resume (maybe exaggerate) ● Always ask some questions when they ask if you have some and show interest. ● While solving some logical questions, explain your approach and do not stay silent for long. 6 ● Go through the geeks for geeks puzzles section : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzles/?ref=shm ● If you don't know something state it and then maybe try to attempt it ● Prepare a proper introduction excluding just your educational details. All the best! 7
